I've been working this land for 10 years and I know what it takes in Quzhou. The soil here is decent — flat North China Plain ground with reliable well access. My wife handles most of the off-farm work so I do most of the field labor myself, sometimes with help from my parents when it's busy season. I need to keep costs reasonable but I'm not going to cut corners that hurt yield — grain prices haven't been great but my family depends on this.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant around mid-October on all 5 mu. I use improved varieties recommended by the county ag station — I've tried a few and settled on ones that do well here. I apply base fertilizer before plowing, then topdress with urea at jointing. Three irrigations is my standard: one before the ground freezes, one at jointing, one at heading. I spray herbicide in early spring and do a combined fungicide-insecticide pass around heading to protect against rust and aphids. Rotary tillage after maize harvest is what I always do — keeps the soil loose without going too deep.

**Maize (summer):** Right after I harvest wheat in June, I direct-seed maize. No-tillage saves me time and fuel and the moisture stays in better. I use a hybrid — Zhengdan 958 type — everyone around here does and the yields are solid. I topdress nitrogen in two shots: once at jointing, once at big bell stage. Summer rains help a lot but I irrigate once at emergence if it's dry and once around tasseling to be safe.
